title: Validate the whole load before the first write
original:
## S1: Validate the whole load before the first write

Old complexity. Refusals are spread over the write sequence of `LoadNewModule` (`src/cls/IPM/Utils/Module.cls:1152-1364`). Path checks run in `Main:LoadInternal`. The downgrade and update-required guards run inside the transaction (`:1213-1222`). The no-transaction marker sets `Committed` before the manifest import (`:1224-1227`). Manifest validation happens inside and after `$system.OBJ.Load` (`:1251-1264`). System requirements are checked after the developer-mode commit (`:1321`). So whether a refusal writes anything depends on the mode and on which check fires.

What gets simpler. Read the manifest once (`GetModuleObjectFromPath`, `:1164`). Name the log. Run every refusal on the in-memory object: path, manifest validity, downgrade, update-required, system requirements, and the developer-mode overwrite guard. Only then start the transaction or set the no-transaction marker. Every refusal then writes nothing in every mode, and the record names the package.

Preserved behavior. Developer mode keeps the manifest and phase work of an installable module that fails later (B1-C26). Same-version loads succeed (B1-C19). A refusal still reads `Committed=0`.

Decisive neighboring pair. B1-C23 (system requirements refused under `-dev`) today keeps the manifest. Under S1 it must leave the namespace unchanged. B1-C26 (`-dev` Activate failure) must keep its manifest and resources as today.

Policy choice. Adopting S1 answers Q-17 with option A ("check system requirements before any write"). It does not make the question moot. If the maintainers choose option B (requirements may be checked after a developer-mode commit), S1 must keep that one check where it is.

Tradeoffs. A manifest read twice (once in memory, once by `OBJ.Load`) must not diverge. Validation that depends on the imported document (multiple documents, B1-C51/C52) has to run against the parsed file instead.

Evidence. Not modeled as a variant. The L1 contract already encodes the required outcome. The cases it would change are B1-C08, C09, C10, C11–C15, C18, C23, C24, C51 and C52 (re-evaluated in `FR/20261114T002646Z-final-replay-reeval/delta.md`). Native B2-B4 and g3 show today's behavior.
cost_review: Validation moves to a preflight reader. It still must check parsed documents, mutable input consistency, imported requirements and developer-mode refusal policy; no comparable full preflight Verus variant exists.

title: One durable history row per action
original:
## S2: One durable history row per action

Old complexity. A log has an IRISTEMP copy and a namespace twin. The twin is written at `Init` (`src/cls/IPM/General/HistoryTemp.cls:9-26`) and from `%OnClose` (`:30-70`). Whether it survives depends on the transaction level at those two moments and on when IRIS runs `%OnClose` (premises P-06a–c). A dependency's log is created and closed inside its parent's transaction, so a parent rollback removes it (D1).

What gets simpler. Every setter writes the durable row directly, with process journaling off for that save (`%IPM.Utils.JournalManager(0)`), so no rollback and no process end can remove it. IRISTEMP becomes a cache. `Committed` is the one field written journaled, set to 1 just before the commit that makes the action's changes durable, as the row's last write before that commit. Any rollback then restores 0. `Finalized` is set only together with `TimeEnd`, so a record whose action never ended stays unfinalized (D27).

Scope of the evidence. The models cover the dependency rows. The top-row part of S2 (D10, D25, D26, D27) is argued from the design and not modeled. In every follow-up variant, an unended top row still reads `Committed=0` with kept writes at many process ends (29,042 end states as built, D26 under Q-08).

Corrections from the follow-up. (Model `models/loadtx.py`, receipt `FR/20261114T004842Z-final-loadtx-model`. Dependency-row counts include unfinished rows, checked under Q-08's provisional answer.)

1. One transaction mode per load. Variant 103 meets every dependency clause only when every activation uses the load's mode. A dependency whose own `<Defaults>` set NoJournal keeps its changes after a parent rollback (the product's behavior, D14), but under S2 its row stays at `Committed=0`. That gives 842 finalized and 1,559 unfinished dependency rows with the wrong `Committed` in REPAIR-103. S2 therefore needs S8, or a rule that marks such a dependency's row committed at its own close.
2. Write ordering at the close. A rollback undoes a journaled write only if the row still holds the value that write set (new premise P-14, native `FR/native/20261113T234716Z-p21-ordering-r2`). IRIS runs `%OnClose` at a Terminate before its rollback (P-06b). If the top-level close finalizes dependency rows with journaling off while the load's transaction is open, a Terminate between the `Committed=1` mark and its commit leaves `Committed=1` on a dependency that was rolled back (60 end states, 30 of them distinct, in variant REPAIR-103). The window is two adjacent statements wide. It follows from the design text "dependency rows are finalized at the top-level close". The original crate's variant 103 models the mark as atomic with the commit and finalizes dependency rows only at a returned close, so it could not show this window. The guarded variant (REPAIR-103-GUARDED) finalizes dependency rows at the close only when no transaction of the load is open. It removes the 60 window states and nothing else: the NoJournal rows it no longer finalizes still read the wrong `Committed` (unfinished NoJournal violations rise from 1,559 to 2,338). A mutant that writes the rows unjournaled between the mark and the commit is detected.
4. A residual every variant keeps. A SIGKILL of a load that runs without a transaction (caller flag or top module defaults), before a dependency's close, leaves that dependency's row at `Committed=0` with its writes kept (9,216 end states). The original handoff named this residual (`handoff.md:80`). Only REPAIR-103-GUARDED-GLOBAL, which also uses one transaction plan per load (S8), has no other dependency-row violation.
3. The premise S2 depends on is now stated precisely. The rollback-proof insert is R-01 (native N-P20). The ordering rule is P-14 (N-P20c, N-P20c2, N-P21A, N-P21R). The original text described the hazard of a journaled insert followed by unjournaled updates (N-P20c2). The follow-up shows the opposite order, an unjournaled write after the journaled mark, is the one that defeats the rollback.

Preserved behavior. Finalized rows stay immutable (`history.locked`). A top-level failure reads `Committed=0`. IDs follow start order. In developer mode, a dependency committed by C2 keeps `Committed=1` when the parent fails later (B1-C38).

Decisive neighboring pair. B1-C31 (default parent fails after its dependency loaded): the dependency row must survive with `Committed=0`. B1-C38 (`-dev` parent fails after C2): the dependency row must read `Committed=1`. The as-built evaluator could not have checked the first one correctly (R02a in `followup/replay/`). The corrected evaluator's control "Committed per slot" does.

Unresolved choices. Whether IPM may write history outside a caller's transaction at all (Q-05, Q-06b). Writing it unjournaled makes the record survive the caller's rollback. Whether that is wanted is a maintainer decision. The rule for dependencies whose own defaults turn journaling off depends on Q-22. The repair design itself is Q-30. What an unfinished record must say is Q-08 and Q-21.

Tradeoffs. IRIS mirroring replicates through the journal, so a history row written with journaling off would not reach a mirror member. Neither the original uplift nor this review tested mirroring, and the update framework distinguishes mirror members (`src/cls/IPM/General/Update/VersionBase.cls`).

Evidence. Original: variant 103, `repair-103-dep-clauses` PASS (189,577 states) and `repair-103-invariants` PASS, rerun on the final inputs (`FR/20261113T233031Z-repair-103-dep-clauses`, `FR/20261113T233031Z-repair-103-invariants`). Follow-up: `FR/20261114T004842Z-final-loadtx-model` variants REPAIR-103, REPAIR-103-GUARDED, REPAIR-103-GUARDED-GLOBAL, REPAIR-103-M-LATE-MARK.
cost_review: Variant 103 covers transactional dependency rows, not the whole top-row/caller/NoJournal/unfinished-row proposal. Guarded/global Python variants have different policy scope. Their state totals cannot be promoted to a comparable Verus state reduction.

title: Mark `Committed` only where a write is kept
original:
## S3: Mark `Committed` only where a write is kept

Old complexity. `Finalize` sets `Committed = Committed || ISOK(status)` (`src/cls/IPM/General/AbstractHistory.cls:127-133`). On the top-level load path this never changes the value, because every successful path already calls `SetCommitted` (original control 05 survives as an equivalent mutant). For a dependency it does change it: a successful dependency closes with `Committed=1` even if its parent later rolls it back. Today D1 hides this because the row is lost.

What gets simpler. `Committed` is written only where a write becomes durable. `uninstall`, which has no transaction and relies on `|| ISOK`, marks it explicitly.

Preserved behavior. A successful top-level load reads `Committed=1`. An uninstall's `Committed` keeps meaning "it succeeded" (`AbstractHistory.cls:41-44`).

Decisive neighboring pair. B1-C31 once its dependency row survives: a successful dependency under a parent that then fails must read 0. B1-C01: a successful top-level load reads 1 through the C3 marker.

Tradeoffs. Every writer that relies on `|| ISOK` has to mark `Committed` itself. `uninstall` is the one known caller, and others outside load and history were not inventoried.

Unresolved choices. Whether `Committed` on an uninstall keeps meaning "it succeeded" or comes to mean "its changes were kept" like the other actions (`history.committed.uninstall`).

Evidence. Follow-up variant REPAIR-NAIVE, which only makes dependency rows survive and keeps today's `Committed` logic, has 2,712 clause violations: rolled-back dependencies read `Committed=1`, through `|| ISOK` and the no-transaction marker. So S3 is required by any D1 repair, not an independent clean-up.
cost_review: Removing the success-based marker requires a complete account of every durable writer and escaped dependency. It is a correctness condition for the history repair, not elimination of an obligation.

title: Structured history filters
original:
## S4: Structured history filters

Old complexity. `ConstructSQLWhere` parses operators out of strings and stops at the first key whose name is not alphanumeric (`src/cls/IPM/General/History.cls:93-126`). Every key after it in collation order is dropped too. An unknown column makes the query fail, and `find` shows an empty listing with an OK status. The retention purge builds its cutoff as a quoted string (`:173`), so its comparison selects nothing.

What gets simpler. Filters are `(column, operator, value)` triples. Columns are checked against the table, including real columns with an underscore such as `Version_Major`. An unknown column is refused with an error. The purge passes a triple with an unquoted cutoff.

Worked preserving and refusing pair (native `FR/native/20261113T234810Z-r04-history-readers`, all read-only except an exact delete of two test rows):

| Case | Filter | Today | Under S4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| N-R04-FIND (preserve) | `Package=fu-hr-a` | 2 rows | 2 rows |
| N-R04-DEL (preserve) | delete `Package=fu-hr-del` | exactly the 2 matching rows deleted, others kept | same |
| N-R04-SEL (real underscore column) | `Version_Major=1`, `package=fu-hr-b` | every row (9) | 1 row |
| N-R04-SEL2 | `Package=fu-hr-b`, `Version_Major=1` | 2 rows (version dropped) | 1 row |
| N-R04-UNKNOWN (refuse) | `NoSuchCol=1` | no rows, status OK | an error naming the column |
| N-R04-CUTOFF (purge selection) | `TimeStart <= cutoff` | quoted cutoff selects 0 rows | the 40-day-old row |

Preserved behavior. Wildcard `*`, the comparison operators, the `-confirm` gate and the SQL-injection guard on column names.

Tradeoffs. Scripts that pass a misspelled or unknown column today get every row back silently. Under S4 they get an error, which is the point but is still a visible change. The purge would start deleting rows on instances where `HistoryRetain` was set long ago and never took effect, so a release note is needed.

Policy choices. Whether default modifiers are filters (Q-18). Under S4 a default modifier that is not a column would be refused, so S4 together with Q-18 option A removes D18. Whether an in-progress record may be purged (Q-20, Q-29). The model shows that once D3 is fixed, an in-progress record older than the cutoff is purged unless S4's purge triple excludes unfinished rows.

Evidence. `models/history_readers.py` (receipt `FR/20261114T002647Z-final-history-readers-model`): the 69 commands of the valid neighbor (plain columns, no default modifiers) match the contract exactly. The deliberately wrong variant "skip invalid keys" (a tempting partial fix) still differs from the contract and is refuted natively by N-R04-SEL. So skipping instead of stopping is not a repair. The variant with an unquoted cutoff is refuted by the archived no-op purge (X4), which confirms the quoting is the cause of D3.
cost_review: The comparison is an executable Python reader model, not an actual paired Verus filter design. Parsing, column validation, typed values and SQL binding remain obligations in a structured representation.

title: One exit path per phase
original:
## S5: One exit path per phase

Old complexity. In `ExecutePhases` a phase's end is recorded in the catch for thrown errors and on the success path (`src/cls/IPM/Storage/Module.cls:692-711`). A returned error status from an Invoke leaves the loop through `quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)` (`:669-671`) and bypasses both, so the phase stays open (D6).

title: A temporary repository that cannot outlive or fail its load
original:
## S7: A temporary repository that cannot outlive or fail its load

Old complexity. Loading a directory registers its `.modules` folder as a filesystem repository with first priority (`OverriddenSortOrder = -1000`, `src/cls/IPM/General/TempLocalRepoManager.cls:28`). It is created before the transaction (`src/cls/IPM/Main.cls:2528`) and removed only by an explicit `CleanUp()` (`TempLocalRepoManager.cls:73`). A cleanup error after the load committed turns a successful load into a reported failure (D13). A process end leaves the repository registered, and it then shadows later dependency resolution (I2).

What gets simpler. Give the temporary repository a name scoped to the process and the load, run its cleanup in a block that cannot change the load's status, and remove leftovers whose owning process no longer exists the next time a repository is resolved.

Preserved behavior. Dependencies in `.modules` are found before every other repository during the load (B1-C30, N-R05-DIA, N-R05-NESTS).

Decisive neighboring pair. B1-C29 (cleanup fails after the commit) must report the load's success with a warning. B1-C30 (normal cleanup) must not change.

Tradeoffs. A sweep needs a reliable "owner is gone" test. Two concurrent loads of the same directory would each need their own repository.

Unresolved choices. Whether a cleanup failure after the commit is reported as a warning or not at all. Whether the sweep runs at every resolution or only at IPM start-up.

title: Namespace-aware history readers and setting scope
original:
## S9: Namespace-aware history readers and setting scope

Old complexity. History IDs restart in each namespace, but the global readers do not carry the namespace. `GlobalRecords` returns no namespace or ID column, and it reads the caller's namespace once per namespace (D20, archived H10). `DeleteHistoryGlobally` ignores every exception in a namespace, not only permission errors (`src/cls/IPM/General/History.cls:199-230`), so a global delete with an unusable column reports "Deleted 0 record(s)" while the local delete fails. "Namespace" default modifiers are stored instance-wide (D19).

What gets simpler. Every global reader row carries `(Namespace, ID)`. A global delete reports each namespace's outcome and skips only namespaces it may not read. Default modifiers are stored per namespace, or documented and named as instance-wide.

Preserved behavior. `history find -globally` already lists rows per namespace correctly (archived H10). The documented global delete without `-confirm` (D block `history.delete.global-unfiltered`) stays.

Decisive neighboring pair. `GlobalRecords` from a namespace with three rows, with a second IPM namespace present, must return every namespace's rows once with their namespace. `history find -globally` must not change.

Tradeoffs. Adding columns to `GlobalRecords` and `Records` changes an `@API.Query` result shape that callers may read by position. Per-namespace default modifiers would change behavior for users who set them once for the whole instance today.

Unresolved choices. Which errors a global delete may skip (Q-27). Whether readers return the namespace and ID (Q-28). Whether IPM's own uninstall may touch other namespaces' records (Q-16).

title: Stage files outside the database until the commit
original:
## S10: Stage files outside the database until the commit

Old complexity. Archive installs and loads replace the module's folder before any version guard (`src/cls/IPM/Main.cls:2507-2509`, `src/cls/IPM/Utils/Module.cls:236-242`), the lock file is written before the parent's commit (OBS-L11), and a git URL load keeps its clone (OBS-L13). A rollback undoes none of these, so a refused or failed load can leave files that do not match the database (I6).

What gets simpler. Unpack or clone into a temporary folder, run every refusal and the load, and move the result into place only after the commit. Remove the temporary folder on failure.

Preserved behavior. A successful archive install leaves the same files in the same place as today.

Decisive neighboring pair. A downgrade refusal from an archive must leave the installed module's folder unchanged. A successful archive install of a newer version must replace it.

Tradeoffs. A move after the commit can itself fail, which leaves a committed module without its files. The move must be retried or reported.

Unresolved choices. What a rollback promises beyond the database (Q-04). If the maintainers decide that files outside the database are not covered, S10 is still a robustness improvement but not a requirement.

Evidence. Not modeled. OBS-L7, OBS-L11 and OBS-L13 are code reading only (`bugs_issues.md` I6).

title: Durable history writes only at `$TLEVEL` 0; reconcile at the next command
original:
## D1. Durable history writes only at `$TLEVEL` 0; reconcile at the next command

**Problem (RC-1, RC-2, RC-4).** The durable history row lives in the namespace database and is written at whatever
transaction level is open (Init, `%OnClose`, `PersistToTwin`), so a rollback takes it with it. `Committed` lives only
in IRISTEMP until `%OnClose`, and an instance crash runs no `%OnClose` and wipes IRISTEMP.

**Design (the `fix` configuration of `models/verus/load_general.rs`).**
1. When `SetCommitted` runs at `$TLEVEL` 0, also save the durable twin at once (`Utils/Module.cls#L1311-L1313`, the
   developer-mode manifest commit, before the next `TSTART`; and the no-transaction path). This is DEC-HIST-2 option A,
   about two lines.
2. Keep dependency rows pending in IRISTEMP. After the parent's outcome is known (after its rollback, or at the next
   command after a crash), re-persist them at `$TLEVEL` 0, with `Committed` taken from **whether the dependency is
   installed at the logged version now**, not from the logged flag. (Keeping the logged flag was the first version of
   this design; the explorer showed it dishonest after a parent rollback.)

**Removes.** F-HIST-1 (dependency rows survive the parent's rollback), F-HIST-2 (developer-mode crash in dependencies),
F-HIST-8 (restart after a developer-mode or no-transaction load). Premises PC, PD and PI are no longer needed.

**Evidence.** Proved: `g_fixed_refines_strict` (any number of dependencies, any prior state, process and instance
crashes, both crash resolutions), `g_instance_crash_honest_when_fixed`. Cross-checked against the fine model on
35,892 configurations with 0 mismatches (`fold_check_general.py`) and explored in section G of `explore.py`
(`fix-dev-persist`, `fix-dep-repersist`). Not implemented or run in IPM (TRUST.md T18).

**Limits that remain, proved.**
- `g_instance_crash_loses_pending`: an instance crash after a dependency load began loses its pending IRISTEMP row,
  for **any** in-process design that keeps pending rows in IRISTEMP. Premise PI-dep stays. Closing it needs a durable
  pending marker written at `$TLEVEL` 0 before the dependency's transaction starts; not modelled (QUESTIONS.md U5).
- P1 (no caller transaction), P2 (a crash rolls back), P3 (the commit window) stay. Under the resolved intents P1
  and P2 describe accepted behaviour (DEC-HIST-4 B, DEC-LOAD-1 A: document them), not defects.
- A dependency loaded and then undone by its parent reads Success = 1, Committed = 0: the documented reading
  (DEC-HIST-1, wiki page 09 "Committed vs. Success").
- A graceful `iris stop` during a load is another instance of RC-2 (`r4-hist-graceful-stop-txn-after`): step 1 covers
  developer-mode and no-transaction loads; for a transactional load the window between `TCOMMIT` and the twin save
  remains, as in F-HIST-7.

**Simpler than today.** One rule ("durable history is written only at `$TLEVEL` 0") replaces the current reliance on
`%OnClose` timing, which differs between method return, process halt, terminal prompt and instance crash.

comparison.metric: The same 10 declared L2 fields occur on both sides (including configuration and four ghost fields, so this is not an independent semantic-state count). The proposed configuration activates the pending Seq<Row> and enables the Reconcile action: one additional active history collection and one additional recovery transition. No field is eliminated.
comparison.preserve: Per-action success versus kept database writes, rollback-surviving history and the named caller/crash boundary.
comparison.cost: Durability is paid for by extra durable writes, a pending dependency collection and reconciliation/version lookup. The instance-loss-of-pending theorem remains; a durable pending marker is not modeled. Caller transactions, terminal commit and commit-window assumptions are not removed. The fresh full-file run has 37 verified and 2 resource-limit failures, so this audit does not claim a complete green re-verification.

The instance-loss-of-pending theorem remains; a durable pending marker is not modeled. Caller transactions, terminal commit and commit-window assumptions are not removed. The fresh full-file run has 37 verified and 2 resource-limit failures, so this audit does not claim a complete green re-verification.

title: Never drop a `%Status`
original:
## D2. Never drop a `%Status`

**Problem (RC-5).** Statuses are discarded in three ways: a status method is called with `do`; `set tSC = $$$OK`
follows the call; or a timeout returns the `$$$OK` the variable was initialised with.

| Site | Defect |
|---|---|
| `Storage/Module.cls#L105-L108` lock timeout returns `sc = $$$OK` | F-INST-1 |
| `Main.cls#L3885-L3886` `do $system.OBJ.LoadStream(...)` | F-NSP-1 |
| `ResourceProcessor/Default/Document.cls#L256-L257` status overwritten | F-RES-1 |
| `Main.cls#L2063-L2093` `do UpdateOne/PrintOne/ResetToDefault` | F-REPO-8 |
| `Main.cls#L2358`, `Utils/Module.cls#L2409` clone return code unchecked | F-LOAD-1 |
| `Storage/Module.cls#L669`, `#L671` returned error quits before `FinalizePhase` | F-HIST-9 |
| `History.cls` `DeleteHistoryGlobally` swallows per-namespace errors | part of F-HIST-6 |

**Design.** One rule: every `%Status` is either returned, combined (`$$$ADDSC`), or written to the history and turned
into a non-OK command status. Aggregate commands (`enable -community`, `sync` with no module) return an error when any
part fails (DEC-NSP-4, DEC-SYNC-3 decide whether that is wanted). Enforce with a lint over `do ##class(...).<m>(...)`
and `do ..<m>(...)` where `<m>` returns `%Status`, and over `set tSC = $$$OK` directly after `set tSC = ...`. For
F-HIST-9, call `FinalizePhase` in a `finally`-style path shared by the catch and the early quit.

**Evidence.** F-INST-1 is premise-scoped: `inst_refines` proves every update step meets L1 under PL (the lock is
granted); making the timeout an error removes the only case PL excludes. The others are inspection plus IRIS.

**Resolved intents.** A busy update lock fails the update with a clear error (DEC-INST-6, assumption from the PR #887
authors' removed `TestSimultaneousUpdateFails`); `config` errors return an error status (DEC-REPO-4); a failed
`enable -community` step fails the command (DEC-NSP-4, assumption); `reload` of a module without a root says nothing
was loaded (DEC-SYNC-4, assumption). `sync` with no module name keeps reporting each failure and returning OK
(DEC-SYNC-3, assumption), so it is not changed.
cost_review: A slogan covering unrelated error sites does not remove their independent status obligations. Each producer/caller still needs checked propagation and a supported failing input.

title: Check before acting in Clean; "skipped" is its own outcome; fail closed
original:
## D3. Check before acting in Clean; "skipped" is its own outcome; fail closed

**Problem (RC-6).** `ExecutePhases` calls every resource processor's `OnBeforePhase("Clean")` (web and CSP
applications deleted, files purged, `Unconfigure` hooks run) before `%Clean` asks `CheckBeforeClean` whether the
module may be removed at all. When the check says no, the command still returns OK and logs a successful uninstall.
The dependents check also ignores modules whose dependency graph failed to build.

**Design.**
1. Run the dependents and global-scope check first, before any `OnBeforePhase("Clean")`, for the top module and for
   each dependency in `-r`.
2. A blocked top-level uninstall returns an error naming the dependents and logs a failed uninstall (DEC-UNIN-1,
   resolved from issue #58 and IPM's skipped `TestUninstallDependencyDoesError`). Inside `-r`, keeping a need that
   another module still uses stays a success, but must not delete the need's web applications.
3. Fail closed: if any installed module's graph cannot be built, treat it as a possible dependent (or fail the
   command and name it), instead of dropping it.

**Removes.** F-UNIN-1, F-UNIN-6, F-UNIN-4.

**Evidence (premise-scoped).** `unin_refines_blocked_unchanged` (premises PG, PW), `unin_refines_clean_keeps_target`
(PCW, PF), `unin_refines_dependents_protect` (PG), `unin_refines_honest` and `unin_refines_rows_honest` (PB, PG, PI,
PNF; PR). PW/PCW exclude modules with web apps, PG excludes failed graphs, PB excludes blocked uninstalls: exactly the
defect cases. Explorer: `repo-explore-unin-blocked-unchanged`, 0 violations under the premises, 271,984 without.

**Note.** IPM's test `PublishModuleWithDeps.cls#L25-L26` asserts the current success; it predates the block and must
change, and `TestUninstallDependencyDoesError` can then be unskipped.

title: Identify IPM by resolved module, not by typed name; normalise names once
original:
## D4. Identify IPM by resolved module, not by typed name; normalise names once

**Problem (RC-7).** The self-uninstall guard runs only when the typed name is exactly `zpm` (`Main.cls#L2712`), but
lookups are case-blind and accept the external name `IPM`. The recursive clean of `-r` never reaches that guard at
all. `list-dependents` compares the typed name with lower-cased graph keys.

**Design.**
1. Resolve the typed name to a module record once, at the command boundary (case-blind name, then external name), and
   pass the record on.
2. Put the self-uninstall guard on the resolved record ("this is IPM's own record"), inside the Clean path, so it
   covers `uninstall IPM`, `uninstall ZPM` and IPM reached as a dependency in `-r` (refuse to remove IPM there, or
   ask).
3. `list-dependents` and every other name comparison use the resolved, lower-cased name.

**Removes.** F-UNIN-3, F-UNIN-8, F-DEP-3, and F-UNIN-11: with the guard keyed on "IPM is really being removed",
`zpm clean` becomes an ordinary level-0 Clean with no orphan warning (DEC-UNIN-2).

**Evidence (premise-scoped).** `unin_refines_self_guard` under PN (the operator types exactly `zpm`) and
`unin_refines_ipm_kept` under PI (IPM is not a dependency removed by `-r`); both premises name the defect cases.
IRIS: `nc-unin-env-name-case` shows the lookups are case-blind.
cost_review: Resolved identity must be available before self-removal and recursion; normalization does not settle externally named aliases or remove privileged cleanup checks.

title: One ordered registry selection used by every command
original:
## D5. One ordered registry selection used by every command

**Problem (RC-9, plus inconsistent `Enabled` checks).** Install collects candidates in a subscript keyed by registry
ID, so the creation order beats `OverriddenSortOrder`. Publish reads only the first row of a per-kind query that has no
`ORDER BY`, so the publish flag on a newer registry is ignored, and falls back to any registry with credentials when
no registry has the flag. `search` and `publish -r` ignore `Enabled`; install and unpublish honour it.

**Design.** One query (or one method) returns enabled registries in a total order: (publish flag where publishing),
sort order, name, ID. Every command (install, search, publish, unpublish) uses it, so `Enabled` and the order are
applied in one place. With no flagged registry, the fallback (token, then user and password, then any) is kept: it
is intended (DEC-REPO-1, PR #332); the help text changes instead. Disabled registries are never used, by any command
(DEC-REPO-2); `repo -list` still shows them.

**Removes.** F-INST-4, F-REPO-10 (restoring the `ORDER BY PublishOrder, ID` that commit `3174d72d` dropped), F-REPO-7.

**Evidence (premise-scoped).** `repo_refines_publish_default` under PH, PU, PK (PK excludes F-REPO-10, PH excludes
F-REPO-3), `repo_refines_publish_named` and `repo_refines_search` under PE (PE excludes F-REPO-7);
`repo_install_enabled_only` (no premise) shows install already honours `Enabled`. Note from the decisions file:
the order alone fixes F-REPO-10.
cost_review: Shared selection still needs different search, publication and unpublication policies and provider order. Those obligations move to the shared selector; no complete proposed Verus selector was supplied.

title: Select update step classes by exact name `V<digits>`
original:
## D6. Select update step classes by exact name `V<digits>`

**Problem.** `GetUpdatePackageClassList` takes every class whose name starts with `<UpdatePackage>.V`, strips
everything but digits, and keys the list by that number. `V3Helper` overwrites `V3`; `Validator` gives an empty
subscript and `<SUBSCRIPT>`.

**Design.** Match the last name piece against `V` followed only by digits (`?1"V"1.N`); ignore other classes. Reject
(with the class name) two step classes with the same number, e.g. `V3` and `V03`.

**Removes.** F-INST-6, F-INST-7.

**Evidence.** Proved witnesses `inst_witness_helper_class_hides_steps`, `inst_witness_class_without_number_fails`; the
L1 rule "every step class is walked" holds once the list contains only `V<digits>` classes (the model's class list is
the only input that differs). IRIS probes in `65-inst-model-order.log`.
cost_review: Exact-name parsing repairs class discovery but adds the obligation to define/refuse legacy helper names. The as-built witness is not a proved after parser.

title: Resolve developer mode once, at the command boundary
original:
## D7. Resolve developer mode once, at the command boundary

**Problem (RC-11).** The effective developer mode is decided in several places: the typed `-dev`/`-nodev`, the mode
stored on the module, `LoadModuleReference` forcing 0 for non-snapshot registry versions, `LoadModuleFromDirectory`
overriding it for every load that is not a top-level install, and `Main:Install` passing `DeveloperMode=0`. The
update guard reads only the typed flag; seeding reads only the stored flag.

**Design.** Compute one value at the command boundary (typed flag, else stored mode, else 0) and pass it down; the
registry rule (dependencies from a registry load in normal mode) applies to dependencies only, never to the named
module.

Add one seeding rule: whenever a module version arrives without its update steps being run (any install, a dev
install, or a module that an update brings in for the first time), seed the steps of every version up to it
(DEC-INST-2, DEC-INST-8, assumptions). Extend the dev-mode guard to needed modules: refuse to replace a dependency
that is in developer mode, naming it (DEC-INST-3, assumption; wiki Concepts). Keep the `-dev` bypass of the update
guard and document it (DEC-INST-1, evidence), and keep developer mode on a plain `load` (DEC-LOAD-2, evidence).

**Removes.** F-INST-5, F-INST-8, F-INST-9, F-INST-10.

**Evidence (premise-scoped).** `update_steps.rs` proves every step meets L1 under PF5 ("the run has the typed flag,
else the stored mode"), which is exactly this design; PF5 fails today only for registry loads
(`inst-explore-refinement-without-pf5`, 76,348 violating transitions).
cost_review: Moving flags to the command boundary does not preserve stored mode, dependency defaults and step-seeding policy without owner decisions. Those obligations remain at the boundary.

title: Stage file-system effects and apply them after the database outcome
original:
## D8. Stage file-system effects and apply them after the database outcome

**Problem (RC-6 for files).** File effects are never rolled back. An archive load deletes and recreates
`<ModuleRoot>/<name>/<version>/` before any check; a URL load clones into `mgr/Temp/...` and points the module Root
there; `install -create-lockfile` writes the lock file before the module's own Activate.

**Design.** Extract, clone or write into a staging folder; after the database commit, move it into place (or record
the final path); after a rollback, delete the staging folder. Check the clone's return code (D2).

**Removes.** F-LOAD-3, F-LOAD-2, F-LOAD-1 (with D2), F-DEP-8 (write the lock file only after the whole install
succeeds, as PR #963's author described; DEC-DEP-2).

**Evidence.** IRIS observations of each case; not modelled. Committed covers database changes only (DEC-HIST-5,
resolved from PR #578); with staging, file changes also follow the database outcome, so history and disk agree.
cost_review: Staging files adds a durable stage, commit/rename/failure cleanup and crash recovery. Database and filesystem effects remain non-atomic; no after Verus model includes those obligations.

title: One mapping helper with one signature; decide from the planned state
original:
## D9. One mapping helper with one signature; decide from the planned state

**Problem (RC-8, RC-9).** `RemoveRoutineMapping`'s third parameter is the routine type, `RemovePackageMapping`'s is
skip-activation; `AddGlobalMapping`'s fourth is set-collation, its fifth skip-activation. Two call sites pass the flag
in the wrong slot. Separately, the `-repos` step decides with the *active* mapping while new mappings wait for one
batch activation at the end, and the "source" of a mapped namespace is chosen as the last namespace by name sharing
the database.

**Design.**
1. One helper, `Map(kind, ns, name, dest, skipActivation)` / `Unmap(kind, ns, name, skipActivation)`, for package,
   routine and global mappings, so the flag is always in the same slot (or named arguments via an object).
2. Decide the repo step from the planned set of mappings (the batch being built), not from the active configuration.
3. A namespace is a source only if its own routine database holds `%IPM` (DEC-NSP-6, assumption).

**Removes.** F-NSP-6, F-NSP-8 (part 1), F-NSP-4 (part 2), F-NSP-7 (part 3); with the rule below, F-NSP-5.

**Evidence (premise-scoped).** `nsp_lemma_unmap` under RTN and INFO, `nsp_lemma_enable` and `nsp_lemma_community`
under REPOS, and the UNIQ premise for F-NSP-7; each premise names the defect case. IRIS slot probe
`nc-nsp-model-env-rtn-slot` (with type ALL the mapping is removed).

F-NSP-5 (installer in a mapped namespace), resolved intent (DEC-NSP-1, DEC-NSP-2, evidence: PR #485, README#L69):
a namespace that gets IPM by mapping must be unmapped before it gets its own IPM, and repo settings are mapped only
together with the code. So the installer and `load` of IPM refuse while `%IPM` is mapped (as `install zpm` already
does), and part 1 above must make `unmap` complete, since after `unmap` the `install zpm` guard still refuses today
(`r4-nsp-unmap-then-install-guard`).
cost_review: A shared mapping signature does not remove pending-versus-active state, activation failures, collation and source ambiguity. A whole-configuration after model is absent.

title: Record the sync baseline wherever source reaches the server
original:
## D10. Record the sync baseline wherever source reaches the server

**Problem.** The rule "an unmarked baseline equals the server copy" is kept only by `sync` itself. `compile`,
`load -dev` and `reload` put source on the server without updating the baseline or setting a retry mark when they
fail; a module with no baseline has its first sync stamp the disk as baseline without loading.

**Design.** One function, called by every loader (sync, compile, `load -dev`, `reload`), records what reached the
server: the new hash on success, a retry mark on failure. `load -dev -skip-sync` stamps the baseline at load time
(the bytes it loaded), so the first sync compares against what is on the server.

**Removes.** F-SYNC-1 (DEC-SYNC-1, assumption). The `-skip-sync` stamping change above is **not** wanted: the first
sync only records a baseline by design (DEC-SYNC-2, evidence), so F-SYNC-2 is fixed in the help text instead.

**Evidence (premise-scoped).** `sync_lemma_sync`, `sync_lemma_compile`, `sync_lemma_reload` prove L1 under OUT (no
loader outside sync puts non-baseline bytes on the server) and BASE; the design makes both premises true by
construction. Fine-model refinement: 0 violations on premise-respecting traces.
cost_review: A common baseline writer still needs failed-import retry semantics, exact-byte revert and unrelated-server edits. No paired after Verus model covers all of these callers.

title: Remove or implement half-built options
original:
## D11. Remove or implement half-built options

**Problem (RC-10).** Options that are documented and accepted but do nothing are worse than missing options: the
operator believes they worked.

| Option | Today | Simplest honest fix |
|---|---|---|
| `uninstall -purge` (F-UNIN-2) | nothing reads `Purge` | pass the `e` flag to `$system.OBJ.Delete` when set (IRIS `nc-unin-env-obj-delete-e-flag`), or remove the option |
| `-token-auth-method` for remote (F-REPO-1) | ignored | read it in `Remote/Definition:OnConfigure` as ORAS does, or reject it for remote |
| `-sslconfig`, `-publish-url` (F-REPO-2) | ignored | implement, or remove from help and reject |
| `repo -type <bad>` (F-REPO-9) | silently dropped, then a prompt | fail with the existing "Invalid type" message; never prompt when not interactive |
| `PermitDowngrade` (F-DEP-1) | resolver allows, loader refuses | remove the flag, or make the loader honour it |
| `register` phase (F-RES-2) | listed in help and phase lists, no `%Register` | remove from help, `GetCompletePhasesForOne` and `MatchSinglePhase`, or implement |
| Primary-only steps on role change (F-INST-2, now documentation) | comment only | fix the `VersionBase.cls#L18` comment (DEC-INST-7, resolved: mirroring is future work) |
cost_review: Removing an accepted option changes the public interface; implementing it adds its advertised obligation. Neither alternative is a measured behavior-preserving simplification.

title: Reuse existing helpers instead of near-duplicates
original:
## D12. Reuse existing helpers instead of near-duplicates

| Defect | Existing helper that already does it right |
|---|---|
| F-NSP-2 `CheckIPMVersion` reads the current namespace only | `GetIPMVersionInfo` (`Main.cls#L984-L1013`) already resolves a mapped namespace's IPM |
| F-UNIN-9 `-r` deletes a dependency's record with `NameDelete`, leaving its manifest | `%IPM.StudioDocument.Module:Delete` (used for the top module) deletes both |
| F-UNIN-10 full cleanup kills only `CacheD` | kill the class's whole extent (`%KillExtent`) or all three storage globals |
| F-HIST-6 auto-purge quotes the value | `ConstructSQLWhere` already binds it; pass the raw date |
| F-NSP-9 `${ipmdir}` not expanded on the 0.7 upgrade path | the normal install path's placeholder expansion |
| F-RES-1, F-NSP-1 | the local-file branch of `EnableIPM` (`Main.cls#L3904-L3917`) already keeps every status |
| F-REPO-11 ORAS keeps credentials on a URL change | the remote registry's `OnConfigure` (`Remote/Definition.cls#L81-L86`) already clears them; share it |
cost_review: Helpers retain differences in namespace ownership, authentication and manifest cleanup. Reuse alone gives no model reduction; the proposal has no complete paired after model.

title: Small local fixes with no shared pattern
original:
## D13. Small local fixes with no shared pattern

| Defect | Fix |
|---|---|
| F-REPO-4 `config delete` restores the first value set | seed a factory default for every key in the installer; never infer a default from the first set |
| F-REPO-5 default modifiers shared by all namespaces | store them in a non-`%` global (per namespace, as documented), or change the help to say instance-wide |
| F-RES-3 `makedeployed` in dev mode deploys | honour the message: report only, unless packaging (DEC-RES-3 decides packaging) |
| F-RES-4 package path shown only with `-v` | drop the `:tVerbose` condition, as the comment says |
| F-RES-7 tar names ≥ 100 characters cut | use the ustar `prefix` field (paths up to 255) or a GNU long-name header |
| F-RES-8 nested `-quiet` | the suppressor restores the previous device instead of closing a shared null device |
| F-UNIN-5 name-only global resources kept | derive the global from the resource name when `Global` is not set |
| F-UNIN-7 `orphans` lists IRIS items | apply the mapped/system filters to every document type, or default to `CLS` |
| F-DEP-2 lock file in name order | write dependencies as an ordered array in install order |
| F-HIST-5 records without a name | call `SetName` from the manifest read before the guards (DEC-HIST-3, evidence: wiki 09) |
| F-REPO-12 ORAS unpublish of a deployed version | delete the plain tag and every `V__<platform>` tag of that version (DEC-REPO-5, assumption) |
| F-DEP-9 lock file with a folder-loaded need | write the entry with an empty registry, as already done for the base module (DEC-DEP-3, assumption) |
| F-NSP-3, F-RES-5, F-RES-6, F-DEP-4, F-DEP-5 | documentation and comment edits only |
cost_review: This groups unrelated local repairs. It is not one comparable design; fields/obligations cannot be summed across different domains as one simplification.

title: Nothing that can fail runs after the final commit
original:
## D14. Nothing that can fail runs after the final commit

**Problem (RC-12).** `LoadNewModule` commits and sets Committed, then, inside the same `try`, evaluates the
after-install message (`%EvaluateMacro`), and by code reading cleans `.modules` and collects analytics. A throw there
reports the command as failed with every change kept (F-LOAD-4; seen in all three modes). The model premise PM
("nothing fails after the final commit") is false.

**Design.** Evaluate the after-install message (and anything else that can fail) **before** the final commit, or run
post-commit work in its own `try` whose failure is printed as a warning and never changes the command's status or the
history record. Also delete `%IPM.Generated.MacroEval` when its compile fails.

**Removes.** F-LOAD-4, and with it premise PM in the load/history proofs.
cost_review: The as-built model or narrower repair boundary does not contain a comparable after design for the whole proposal. The same callers, provider failures, public interface and policy exceptions still require obligations; moving the check to a shared helper does not eliminate them. Preserve every successful/allowed neighbor named in the original proposal. No complete preservation theorem or source-supported reduction count was found, so the simplification claim is withdrawn.

title: Check every requirement before any commit, in every mode
original:
## D15. Check every requirement before any commit, in every mode

**Problem.** In developer mode the manifest is committed (`Utils/Module.cls#L1311`) before `CheckSystemRequirements`
(`#L1321`) runs, so a module refused by a system requirement stays installed (F-NSP-12).

**Design.** Run `CheckSystemRequirements` (and every other refusal check) before the developer-mode manifest commit.
The intent that a refused load leaves no module, in every mode, is taken from issue #106, the changelog ("prevent
installation") and the wiki ("validated before module installation") (DEC-NSP-5, assumption).
cost_review: The as-built model or narrower repair boundary does not contain a comparable after design for the whole proposal. The same callers, provider failures, public interface and policy exceptions still require obligations; moving the check to a shared helper does not eliminate them. Preserve every successful/allowed neighbor named in the original proposal. No complete preservation theorem or source-supported reduction count was found, so the simplification claim is withdrawn.

title: Use the backtracking resolver
original:
## D16. Use the backtracking resolver

**Problem.** The resolver is greedy and fails on solvable inputs (F-DEP-7); upstream knows it (issue #1299, open) and
has a fix in review (PR #1303, open). Its method comment already promises backtracking.

**Design.** Adopt real backtracking (the open PR or equivalent). The proofs here show a successful resolution is
always sound (`dep_refines`) and every failure names a reason (DEP-B54); after the change, the completeness check
`dep-explore-completeness` (2,040 of 70,656 instances fail today) is the acceptance test.
cost_review: The upstream repair changes repository result cardinality so resolution can consider alternatives. Search-space/caching/provider obligations grow or move; the witness in dep_resolve is not the complete upstream after design.

title: Run the legacy-record migration wherever IPM is enabled
original:
## D17. Run the legacy-record migration wherever IPM is enabled

**Problem.** `EnableIPM` (`Main.cls#L3553-L3708`) never runs `MigrateZPMToIPM`; only an IPM load does. A namespace that
reaches IPM by `enable -map`/`-community` keeps legacy ZPM module records that IPM does not list (F-NSP-10; observed
with a simulated legacy install).

**Design.** Call the same migration (`%IPM.Utils.Migration` `RunAll`) for each target namespace in `EnableIPM`, as a
maintainer required in issue #470 (DEC-NSP-3).
cost_review: Migration adds a writer wherever enable reaches legacy records and must preserve mappings, schema compatibility and partial-failure behavior. No paired after Verus migration model exists.
